title: FOCUS ON The Common GOOD: GROUP DISTRIBUTIONAL ROBUSTNESS FOLLOWS
measurement_description: The paper evaluates worst-group accuracy for a toxicity classification task using the CivilComments-WILDS dataset. One of the demographic groups within this dataset is defined by the mention of terms related to 'muslim'. The evaluation, therefore, measures performance disparity for this specific religious identity group.
findings: On the CivilComments dataset, which includes 'muslim' as a demographic identity group, robust optimization methods significantly improved worst-group accuracy compared to standard Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM). Group-DRO achieved the highest worst-group accuracy (70.0), followed closely by the proposed CGD algorithm (69.1), while the baseline ERM scored much lower (56.0).
